mainTopic: The added fifth (חומש): how it is calculated, whether it holds back redemption, and whether it follows the rules of the main payment
overview: This amud finishes a משנה (from ערכין) about an owner who redeems his own הקדש while someone else bids against him. Its numbers prove that the added fifth (חומש) is counted 'from outside' (מלבר), a quarter of the principal, which matches רבי יאשיה against רבי יונתן. The גמרא then asks whether an unpaid חומש holds back the redemption of מעשר שני. רבינא proves from the rule about דמאי that it does not. The גמרא suggests that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about this, but רב פפא explains that their argument is only about worrying the person will be careless. רבי יוחנן's rule about הקדש is challenged from a ברייתא and narrowed so that it applies only on שבת. Finally, רמי בר חמא asks three questions about whether the חומש follows the rules of the main payment. רבא answers from the word ״עליו״ that it does, and רבינא supports him from a משנה about stolen תרומה.

steps.title: The owner pays the outside bid plus his own fifth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. When another bidder offers 21, 22, 23 or 24, the owner pays that bid plus five.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the other person offers 21, the owner gives 26. If 22, the owner gives 27. If 23, the owner gives 28. If 24, the owner gives 29.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a משנה (in ערכין) it began quoting earlier. The owner offered twenty for his own הקדש item, and now another person outbids him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner's own offer of twenty makes him owe a חומש of five. When someone outbids him, he must match the higher bid, and he still adds the five he owes because of his own offer. So each outside bid simply gets five added on top.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner (the person who made the item הקדש)
Give, pay
The added fifth that an owner pays when he redeems his own הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: The five added each time is not a fifth of the new bid. It is the fixed חומש the owner owes because of his own original offer of twenty.

phrases.english: the owner gives twenty-six.
phrases.notes: This is the answer to a bid of twenty-one, which appears just before this point in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁנַיִם – הַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין עֶשְׂרִים וָשֶׁבַע.
phrases.english: If twenty-two, the owner gives twenty-seven.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְשָׁלֹשׁ – הַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה.
phrases.english: If twenty-three, the owner gives twenty-eight.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע – הַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין עֶשְׂרִים וָתֵשַׁע.
phrases.english: If twenty-four, the owner gives twenty-nine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a משנה the גמרא began quoting before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner pays the highest outside bid plus the five of חומש from his own original offer of twenty.

steps.title: At a bid of twenty-five, the owner pays thirty
steps.stepSummary: If the outside bid is 25, the owner pays 30, because the חומש is never figured on the other bidder's increase.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the other person offers 25, the owner gives 30, because we do not add a fifth based on the raise this other person made.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its last case, a bid of twenty-five, and explains the reason behind all the numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner's חומש is fixed by his own offer, not by anyone else's raise. That is why the owner always adds exactly five, even when the bid goes up to twenty-five.

keyTerms.meaning: Add
A raise or increase in the bid

phrases.english: If twenty-five, the owner gives thirty,
because we do not add a fifth
on the raise of this one.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the other bidder who raised the price.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מוֹסִיפִין חוֹמֶשׁ עַל עִילּוּי שֶׁל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of cases and gives the reason for them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חומש is calculated only on the owner's own offer, never on the other bidder's increase.

steps.title: Proof that the fifth is counted from outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from the משנה that חומש is 'from outside' (מלבר), and confirms it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that the fifth is counted from outside. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the numbers in the משנה to settle its earlier question: is חומש counted 'from inside' or 'from outside'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner's offer of twenty brought a חומש of five, for a total of twenty-five. Five is a quarter of twenty but a fifth of twenty-five. So חומש means one fifth of the final total, which is 'from outside' (מלבר).

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; we can prove from this
From outside: a fifth of the final total, which equals a quarter of the principal

steps.whatToRemember: חומש מלבר: the added fifth makes the principal into four parts out of five. 20 + 5 = 25.

phrases.english: Learn from it: the fifth is from outside.
Yes, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the numbers in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That חומש is calculated from outside (a quarter of the principal).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's numbers: an offer of 20 plus a חומש of 5 adds up to 25.

steps.title: The same question is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that 'inside or outside' is argued by רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים. The פסוק says 'And he shall add its fifth to it.' רבי יאשיה says the item and its fifth together make five parts. רבי יונתן says 'its fifth' means a fifth of the principal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the question it just answered was already argued by two תנאים in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה says the principal plus the חומש total five parts, so חומש is from outside. This matches the משנה we just learned. רבי יונתן says it is a fifth of the principal itself, which is from inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute between תנאים
'And he shall add its fifth to it' (the source in the פסוק)
The principal, the base value

phrases.english: Like a dispute of תנאים: 'And he shall add its fifth to it',
meaning that it and its fifth together are five,
these are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.
Rabbi Yonatan says:
'its fifth' means a fifth of the principal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the conclusion just reached to an earlier dispute between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יאשיה: חומש is from outside (principal plus חומש make five parts). רבי יונתן: חומש is a fifth of the principal, from inside.

steps.title: Does an unpaid fifth hold back the redemption?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: does the חומש hold back the redemption, or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: does the fifth hold things back, or does it not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic and asks a question. The next step will lay out the two ways to look at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the question is about redeeming מעשר שני. If someone paid the value but not yet the חומש, is the redemption already complete, or is it held back until the חומש is paid?

keyTerms.meaning: They asked; a question was raised
Holds back; is required for the act to work

phrases.english: They asked: does the fifth hold it back,
or does it not hold it back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the חומש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether failing to pay the חומש stops the redemption from taking effect.

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: Is produce worth four redeemed with four, with the חומש as a separate personal debt? Or is it redeemed only with five?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is produce worth four redeemed with four, and the owner must add the fifth on his own? If so, the fifth does not hold it back. Or maybe produce worth four is redeemed only with five, and the fifth does hold it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two possible ways to understand the question it just asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the redemption itself costs only the value (four), and the חומש is a separate debt on the person, so the produce is redeemed without it. Side two: the full price of redemption is value plus חומש (five), so without the חומש nothing is redeemed. רבינא brings a proof in steps 7-8.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeems
On himself, as his own personal duty
So it turns out; evidently
Or perhaps

phrases.english: Is four redeemed with four,
phrases.notes: Produce worth four coins, redeemed with four coins.

phrases.english: and he adds the fifth as his own personal duty,
so the fifth does not hold it back.
Or perhaps four is redeemed only with five,
and the fifth does hold it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question just asked.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the חומש part of the redemption price itself, or a separate personal debt that comes after the redemption?

steps.title: רבינא brings a משנה about דמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes a משנה: מעשר שני of דמאי has no חומש and no ביעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Come and hear. For דמאי, there is no extra fifth and no clearing out of tithes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא starts a proof to answer the question of step 6. He quotes a משנה saying that דמאי has no חומש and no ביעור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quote alone does not answer the question yet. רבינא will draw an inference from it in the next step. The key fact here is that the rabbis did not require a חומש when redeeming מעשר שני of דמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to answer a question
Produce bought from an unlearned person, where we are not sure it was tithed. The rabbis require tithing it to be safe.
The clearing out of tithes from the house at set times in the שמיטה cycle
An אמורא who brings the proof here

phrases.english: Ravina said: Come and hear:
Demai has no one-fifth,
phrases.notes: He means: when you redeem the מעשר שני taken from דמאי, you do not add a fifth.

phrases.english: and it has no eradication.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to settle the question raised in steps 5-6.
steps.raayaObject: That the חומש does not hold back the redemption
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in דמאי: הדמאי אין לו חומש ואין לו ביעור

steps.title: רבינא's inference: the קרן is required but the חומש is not
steps.stepSummary: Since דמאי still needs the קרן but not the חומש, the rabbis must have copied only the part that holds things back under Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it does have the principal. Why? The principal, which holds back the eating under Torah law, the rabbis also required for דמאי. The fifth, which does not hold back the eating under Torah law, the rabbis did not require for דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא reads between the lines of the משנה. It skips only the חומש, so the קרן is still required. He explains why: the rabbis kept for דמאי only what holds back the redemption under Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חומש also held back the redemption under Torah law, the rabbis would have required it for דמאי too. They dropped it. That shows that under Torah law, paying the קרן alone already lets you eat, and the חומש is a separate debt. This answers step 6: produce worth four is redeemed with four.

keyTerms.meaning: The principal: the basic value of the produce
Holds back: without it, the redemption does not work
Torah law
Rabbinic law

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key principle. When the rabbis model a law on a Torah law, they keep the parts that are essential and may leave out the parts that are not.

phrases.english: But it does have principal.
What is the reason?
The principal, which holds back by Torah law,
exists also by rabbinic law;
the one-fifth, which does not hold back by Torah law,
does not exist by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קֶרֶן יֵשׁ לוֹ. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The חומש does not hold back the redemption under Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: Inference from the difference between קרן and חומש in the דמאי משנה

steps.title: Suggesting the question is an argument between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the question matches a מחלוקת: if someone paid the קרן but not the חומש, may he eat? רבי אליעזר says yes, רבי יהושע says no, and רבי splits between שבת and weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say it is like a dispute of תנאים: If he gave the principal but not the fifth, רבי אליעזר says he may eat, and רבי יהושע says he may not eat. רבי said: רבי אליעזר's view seems right on שבת, and רבי יהושע's view on weekdays.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that our question is really an old argument between תנאים, and it quotes a ברייתא. This sets up the next step, which will look closely at רבי's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר lets him eat after paying only the קרן, so he holds that the חומש does not hold back the redemption. רבי יהושע forbids eating, so he holds that it does. רבי offers a middle path: he follows רבי אליעזר on שבת and רבי יהושע on weekdays.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like a dispute of תנאים: the גמרא suggests the question was already argued in earlier times
He may eat
The words of ... seem right
A weekday, not שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the names. רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) is a third opinion. He is not the same person as רבי אליעזר or רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: Let us say it is parallel to a dispute of tanna'im:

phrases.aramaic: נָתַן אֶת הַקֶּרֶן, וְלֹא נָתַן אֶת הַחוֹמֶשׁ,
phrases.english: If he gave the principal but did not give the one-fifth,
Rabbi Eliezer says: He may eat.
Rabbi Yehoshua says: He may not eat.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Rabbi said: The words of Rabbi Eliezer seem right on Shabbat,
and the words of Rabbi Yehoshua on weekdays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבינא's proof, the גמרא suggests the question is itself a מחלוקת תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Paying the קרן without the חומש: רבי אליעזר permits eating, רבי יהושע forbids, and רבי splits between שבת and weekdays.

steps.title: From רבי's words, they argue on both שבת and weekdays
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי had to pick a side for each case, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע must argue on both weekdays and שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבי said רבי אליעזר's view seems right on שבת, we see that they argue even on weekdays. Since he said רבי יהושע's view seems right on weekdays, we see that they argue even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at רבי's wording. It shows that the two תנאים really argue across the board. Their argument is not only about one special day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר agreed that you may not eat on weekdays, רבי would not need to say רבי יהושע is right on weekdays. The same reasoning works for שבת. So רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע have a basic disagreement that covers every day of the week. The next step suggests what that disagreement is about.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication: we learn it from what was said
They argue

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּאָמַר נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Since he said, 'The words of Rabbi Eliezer seem right on Shabbat,'
it follows that they argue even on weekdays.

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּאָמַר נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּחוֹל,
phrases.english: Since he said, 'The words of Rabbi Yehoshua seem right on weekdays,'
it follows that they argue even on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאָמַר נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּשַּׁבָּת, מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיגִי אֲפִילּוּ בְּחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads רבי's statement from step 9 closely to prove that the תנאים argue in principle.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue in principle about whether the חומש holds back the redemption
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of רבי's split ruling in the ברייתא

steps.title: Suggesting the argument is about whether the חומש holds things back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי אליעזר holds an unpaid חומש does not hold back eating, and רבי יהושע holds that it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? רבי אליעזר holds the חומש does not hold things back, and רבי יהושע holds it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its suggestion from step 9: the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע is exactly our question about whether the חומש holds things back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר lets him eat after paying only the קרן, the חומש must be a separate debt. If רבי יהושע forbids eating, the redemption must not be finished without the חומש. That would make our question from step 6 a known מחלוקת between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: "Isn't it that...?" A way of proposing a reading
Reasoning, line of logic
Holds back, prevents the process from being finished

phrases.english: What, is it not that they argue about this reasoning:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר חוֹמֶשׁ לָא מְעַכֵּב,
phrases.english: that Rabbi Eliezer holds the fifth does not hold things back,
and Rabbi Yehoshua holds the fifth does hold things back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the suggestion begun in steps 9-10 by naming the reasoning behind each side.
steps.raayaObject: Our question of whether the חומש holds back the redemption
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about eating after paying only the קרן

steps.title: רב פפא: they argue about worrying over carelessness
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says everyone agrees the חומש does not hold things back. The argument is whether we worry the person will be careless and never pay it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: No. Everyone agrees the חומש does not hold things back. They argue about whether we worry he will be careless. One holds we worry, and one holds we don't.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא rejects the suggestion and offers a different reason for the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the strict law, both agree the redemption works with the קרן alone. רבי יהושע forbids eating only as a safety step, so the person won't forget the חומש. So the מחלוקת does not answer our question.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone, both sides agree
We are worried about, we take into account
Carelessness, negligence

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהושע holds that the redemption fails. In רב פפא's reading it fully works. He only forbids eating out of worry that the חומש will never get paid.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: No,
everyone agrees the fifth does not hold things back.
And here they argue about whether we worry about carelessness.
One master holds we worry about carelessness.
phrases.notes: This first master is רבי יהושע, who forbids eating until the fifth is paid.

phrases.english: And the other master holds we do not worry about carelessness.
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר, who lets him eat right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading proposed in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argument settles whether the חומש holds back the redemption.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument can be explained by a worry about carelessness, with both sides agreeing the חומש does not hold it back.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: with הקדש everyone agrees the redemption works
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that with הקדש, all agree the redemption works with the קרן alone, because the Temple treasurers will demand the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Everyone agrees that with הקדש, he has redeemed it, since the treasurers will demand payment from him in the marketplace.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן says the argument is only about מעשר שני. With הקדש, everyone agrees he may use it after paying just the קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits רב פפא's idea. The only worry was that he would never pay the חומש. With הקדש, the Temple treasurers collect the debt, so that worry is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Property given to the בית המקדש
Redeemed it, took away its holiness
Temple treasurers who collect money for הקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Everyone agrees with הקדש that he has redeemed it,
phrases.notes: He means when he paid the main price but not the extra fifth.

phrases.english: since the treasurers demand payment from him in the marketplace.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the carelessness reasoning to set a rule for הקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With הקדש, paying the קרן alone redeems it according to everyone, because the treasurers collect the חומש.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows an argument about הקדש too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: a ברייתא has רבי אליעזר and חכמים arguing about paying only the קרן, and רבי sides with רבי אליעזר for הקדש. That suggests חכמים argue about הקדש too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't they argue about הקדש? But a ברייתא teaches: He paid the קרן but not the חומש. רבי אליעזר says he redeemed it, and חכמים say he did not. רבי said: רבי אליעזר seems right about הקדש, and חכמים seem right about מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's claim that everyone agrees about הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי had to choose רבי אליעזר's view for הקדש. That only makes sense if חכמים disagree about הקדש too. So it does not look like everyone agrees about הקדש, as רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: But a ברייתא teaches. Used to bring a source that contradicts a claim
The words of ... seem correct
Here, מעשר שני

phrases.english: And with הקדש they do not argue?
But it was taught: He gave the main price,
but did not give him the fifth,
Rabbi Eliezer says: He redeemed it,
and the Sages say: He did not redeem it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: Rebbi said: The words of Rabbi Eliezer seem right for הקדש,
and the words of the Sages for מעשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that everyone agrees about הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי chose רבי אליעזר's view for הקדש. That means חכמים disagree there too, so there is an argument about הקדש after all.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן said everyone agrees that paying the קרן redeems הקדש. The ברייתא, with רבי's split ruling, seems to show that חכמים argue about הקדש too. Step 16 answers this by narrowing רבי יוחנן's statement to שבת.

steps.title: רבי's ruling shows both sides argue in both cases
steps.stepSummary: From the way רבי decided, we see that רבי אליעזר argues even about מעשר, and חכמים argue even about הקדש. This contradicts רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said רבי אליעזר seems right about הקדש. That means רבי אליעזר also argues about מעשר. רבי also said חכמים seem right about מעשר. That means חכמים also argue about הקדש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge from the ברייתא in step 14. It reads רבי's two-part ruling closely to show that both sides argue in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only need to 'pick a side' where there is a real argument. Since רבי picked רבי אליעזר for הקדש, there must be an argument about הקדש, so חכמים disagree there. That clashes with רבי יוחנן's claim that everyone agrees about הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The words of ... seem right': a ruling formula that picks one side
'It follows that...': an inference drawn from what was said
They argue / disagree
The Sages, the majority view

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּאָמַר נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ –
phrases.english: From the fact that he said, 'The words of Rabbi Eliezer seem right regarding consecrated property,'
it follows that Rabbi Eliezer argues even regarding tithe.
And from the fact that he said, 'The words of the Sages seem right regarding tithe,'
it follows that they argue even regarding consecrated property!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאָמַר נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 14 by spelling out the inference.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim (step 13) that everyone agrees about הקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling that picks a side shows there is a real argument. So חכמים must argue about הקדש too.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's rule restated: agreement only on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יוחנן's statement was really narrower. Everyone agrees that הקדש redeemed on שבת without the חומש is redeemed. The two reasons are עונג שבת and the Temple treasurers' ability to collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if רבי יוחנן said anything, this is what he said: Everyone agrees that on שבת, הקדש that a person redeemed is redeemed. One reason is the פסוק 'and you shall call שבת a delight.' Another reason is that the treasurers will demand the rest from him in the marketplace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by fixing the wording of רבי יוחנן's statement. The agreement is only about שבת, not about הקדש in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On weekdays חכמים may really argue about הקדש, which fits the ברייתא. On שבת, though, everyone agrees the redemption works with the קרן alone. One reason is to let a person enjoy his food on שבת. The other is that the treasurers will make sure the חומש gets paid later.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If it was said, this is how it was said': the גמרא restating a teaching correctly
Everyone agrees
Redeemed: transferred holiness off the item onto money
Enjoyment and delight of שבת
The Temple treasurers who collect money for הקדש

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated like this:
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Everyone agrees that on Shabbat, with consecrated property, he has redeemed it.
phrases.notes: He means that paying just the main amount, without the extra fifth, already counts as a redemption.

phrases.english: One reason: as it is written:
"And you shall call Shabbat a delight."
And furthermore, since the treasurers
demand payment from him in the marketplace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by narrowing רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the teaching in a narrower form
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said everyone agrees about הקדש at all times.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees only on שבת, because of עונג שבת and because the treasurers will collect the rest.
steps.whatToRemember: Final version: on weekdays there is an argument even about הקדש. On שבת everyone agrees הקדש is redeemed with the קרן alone, for two reasons: עונג שבת and the treasurers collecting.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוחנן's original rule still stands. The גמרא replaces it, so the agreement covers only שבת.

steps.title: Can the extra fifth for הקדש be paid with land?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא notes that הקדש cannot be redeemed with land, only with money. He asks whether the חומש may be paid with land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: They taught that הקדש cannot be redeemed with land, because the תורה says 'he shall give the money and it will be his.' What about its extra fifth: can that be redeemed with land?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רמי בר חמא asks whether the חומש must follow the same payment rule as the main redemption amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main amount must be money, as the פסוק says. The question is whether the חומש counts as part of the redemption itself, so it also needs money, or whether it is a separate add-on that can be paid with land.

keyTerms.meaning: Land / real estate
Becomes redeemed (holiness moves off it)
'The Merciful One': a name for God, used when quoting the תורה
Its extra fifth

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ הֶקְדֵּשׁ אֵינוֹ מִתְחַלֵּל עַל הַקַּרְקַע,
phrases.english: They have said that consecrated property is not redeemed with land,
as the Merciful One said:
"And he shall give the money and it shall be his."
Its extra fifth: what is the law, may it be redeemed with land?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the nature of the חומש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the חומש of הקדש follow the 'money only' rule of the קרן?
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: is the חומש just like the קרן, or is it its own separate payment?

steps.title: Can the extra fifth for eaten תרומה be paid with תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: Repayment for תרומה eaten by mistake must come from חולין, according to the פסוק. The question is whether the חומש may be paid with something that is not חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Repayment for תרומה can only be made from חולין, because the תורה says 'he shall give the holy thing to the כהן,' meaning something that can become holy. What about its extra fifth: may it be paid from something that is not חולין?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a parallel second question, built the same way as the הקדש question. It asks whether the חומש of תרומה follows the same rule as the main repayment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main repayment has to be ordinary food that becomes תרומה once it is given. Food that is already תרומה can't 'become holy' again. The question is whether the חומש has the same requirement, or may be paid with תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce given to a כהן
Ordinary, non-holy food or items
Is repaid
Something fit to become holy

phrases.aramaic: תְּרוּמָה אֵינָהּ מִשְׁתַּלֶּמֶת אֶלָּא מִן הַחוּלִּין.
phrases.english: Teruma may be repaid only from non-sacred food,
phrases.notes: This is about a non-כהן who ate תרומה by mistake and has to pay the כהן back.

phrases.english: as the Merciful One said:
"And he shall give the holy thing to the priest":
something that is fit to become holy.

phrases.aramaic: חוּמְשָׁהּ מַהוּ שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּלֵּם שֶׁלֹּא מִן הַחוּלִּין?
phrases.english: Its extra fifth: what is the law, may it be repaid from what is not non-sacred?

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּמְשָׁהּ מַהוּ שֶׁיִּשְׁתַּלֵּם שֶׁלֹּא מִן הַחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel second question, using the same pattern as step 17 but applied to תרומה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the חומש of תרומה have to come from חולין like the main repayment?

steps.title: Can the fifth of מעשר be redeemed with an unminted coin?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא's third question: מעשר itself cannot be redeemed with an unminted coin, so what about its חומש?
steps.simpleTranslation: מעשר cannot be redeemed with an unminted coin. The תורה says ״וצרת הכסף בידך״, which teaches that you need something with an image stamped on it. So what about the extra fifth: may it be redeemed with an unminted coin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the third question in רמי בר חמא's set, this time about מעשר and coins with no stamp. It follows the same pattern as the two questions before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ״וצרת״, which sounds like צורה (image). From this we learn that מעשר must be redeemed with a real minted coin. The question is whether this rule also covers the חומש, or only the main amount (the קרן).

keyTerms.meaning: A blank, unminted coin with no image stamped on it
Is redeemed (its holiness moves onto the money)
An image or stamp, like the design on a minted coin
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳

phrases.english: Tithe cannot be redeemed with an unminted coin.
As the Merciful One said:
"And you shall bind up the money in your hand,"
phrases.notes: דברים 14:25. The word וצרת sounds like צורה (image), and the דרשה is built on that.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו צוּרָה.
phrases.english: to include anything that has an image on it.
Its fifth: what is the law, may it be redeemed with an unminted coin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third parallel question in רמי בר חמא's series, after הקדש with land and תרומה from non-חולין
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חומש of מעשר must follow the main amount's rule of needing a minted coin

steps.title: רבא answers: the fifth is like the main amount
steps.stepSummary: The questions reach רבא, who learns from ״עליו״ that the חומש has the same rules as the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The questions traveled until they came before רבא. He told them: the פסוק says ״עליו״ (unto it). This teaches that the fifth is treated just like the main amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives one answer that settles all of רמי בר חמא's questions at once. The חומש is treated just like the קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״עליו״ connects the fifth to the main payment it is added to. So whatever rule applies to the קרן also applies to the חומש. That means no land for הקדש, payment from חולין for תרומה, and a minted coin for מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter rolled along, meaning the question was passed from person to person
Unto it, the word in the פסוק about adding the fifth
Like it, with the same law

steps.whatToRemember: The חומש follows the same rules as the קרן, because of the word ״עליו״.
steps.whyThisMatters: One general rule answers all three questions together: הקדש, תרומה, and מעשר.

phrases.english: The matter rolled along
and came before רבא.
He said to them: The verse says "unto it,"
to include its fifth as being like it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא עָלָיו לְרַבּוֹת חוּמְשׁוֹ כְּמוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the three questions of רמי בר חמא together
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חומש has the same law as the קרן, learned from ״עליו״

steps.title: רבינא supports רבא from a משנה about stolen תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings a משנה: a thief who eats תרומה pays the קרן and the חומש from חולין. This shows the חומש follows the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: We also learned this in a משנה. If someone steals תרומה and does not eat it, he pays double its value, figured at the price of תרומה. If he ate it, he pays two principals plus a fifth. One principal and the fifth come from חולין, and the other principal is figured at the price of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a משנה that backs up רבא's answer, at least for the case of תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thief who eats תרומה owes two things. As a thief, he owes double. As a non-כהן who ate תרומה, he owes the קרן plus the חומש. The משנה says the קרן and the חומש are both paid from חולין, so the fifth follows the principal, just like רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: We have learned it, in a משנה
Double payment, which a thief owes
The principal, meaning the basic value
Ordinary food that is not holy

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different principals here. One is the thief's extra payment, figured at the cheaper price of תרומה. The other is the payment for eating תרומה, which together with the fifth must come from חולין.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא,
phrases.english: רבינא said: We too have learned this:
One who steals תרומה and did not eat it
pays double payment at the price of תרומה.
If he ate it, he pays two principals and a fifth.
A principal and the fifth from חולין,
and the other principal at the price of תרומה.
phrases.notes: This is the thief's extra payment for stealing, so it can be figured at the cheaper price of תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support רבא's answer
steps.raayaObject: That the חומש follows the קרן and must come from חולין
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in תרומות 6:4 about one who steals and eats תרומה
